messages.author: 4176b8a6b6e182cd
messages.subject: online / live estimation of temporal models (DBNs / HMMs)
parts:
Hey together,

I am new to Stan and the field of probabilistic modeling and I am wondering whether Stan is able to do online inference of temporal models.
I want to create a Dynamic Bayesian Network (generalization to an HMMs) to model a nonlinear state space system (e.g. a motion model) where the control input (e.g. acceleration) is dependent on multiple latent random variables. I want to update this DBN live as new sensor measurements are available (~100 milliseconds).
Do MCMC methods even make sense in that purpose (as of the long burn-in phase), or do I have to stick with sequential Monte Carlo methods (particle filters)?
Furthermore, is it possible to do parameter estimation with both unobserved and observed data with some kind of expectation maximization algorithm within Stan?

Thanks a lot for your help!

I want to update this DBN live as new sensor measurements are available (~100 milliseconds).

In real time? That'd be very ambitious for MCMC if you want
to be sure you've converged and are updating properly.
> Do MCMC methods even make sense in that purpose (as of the long burn-in phase), or do I have to stick with sequential Monte Carlo methods (particle filters)?

Some of the particle filter methods are conjugate, so don't
need any Monte Carlo. Those can work on the time frame
you're talking about.
> Furthermore, is it possible to do parameter estimation with both unobserved and observed data with some kind of expectation maximization algorithm within Stan?

You have to marginalize out the unobserved data yourself,
then use Stan's optimizer. Basically gives you exactly the EM
algorithm, with the M step being done by L-BFGS optimization and
the E step being done in the Stan code. The HMMs in the manual
are examples of how to do the marginalization.

- Bob
